piece.caption: How contractors can dictate site notes using ChatGPT Live Dictation without waiting for audio transcription. OpenAI has rolled out live dictation across web, desktop, iOS, and Android apps on all plans. Instead of waiting for an audio file to process, ChatGPT now generates text in real time as you speak, with the previous 10-minute recording limit removed. You can tap the audio waveform to view and edit text directly in the prompt box before converting it into quotation bullet points. Always double-check measurements before finalizing estimates. piece.dm_text:
Here is how to use ChatGPT Live Dictation for site notes:

1. Open ChatGPT on your mobile app (iOS or Android) or web browser.
2. Tap the microphone icon in the prompt box.
3. Speak your site measurements or client requirements naturally. The text now transcribes live on screen as you speak.
4. Tap or click the audio waveform to inspect the live transcript.
5. The 10-minute limit is now removed, so you can dictate longer walkthroughs.
6. In the prompt box, add: 'Convert these notes into clear bullet points for a quotation draft.'
7. Always verify numbers and dimensions before sending quotations to clients.

Stevie Bonifield Nov 19, 2026, 3:16 PM UTC Link
Stevie Bonifield is a news writer covering all things consumer tech. Stevie started out at Laptop Mag writing news and reviews on hardware, gaming, and AI. ChatGPT can receive audio prompts from your microphone faster now with a Live Dictation feature that transcribes as you speak, rather than waiting until you finish recording. It’s rolling out now globally on all ChatGPT plans on the web, desktop app, and iOS and Android apps. While using dictation in ChatGPT, you can tap or click the audio waveform to show the live text transcript the AI is generating, then edit it in the prompt box when you’re done.
Along with faster transcription, OpenAI also announced it’s removing the 10-minute recording limit on voice dictation in ChatGPT, and it says the feature is getting “more reliable.” The update follows an overhaul for ChatGPT’s two-way conversational voice mode earlier this year. Last year, OpenAI also announced a “record mode” for transcribing voice notes and meetings. That feature is still in beta and limited to Plus, Enterprise, Edu, Business, and Pro workspaces, but you can also use ChatGPT’s prompt box dictation feature to ask it to transcribe voice messages or turn them into bullet points.
